- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 73+ → forecast jumps to 75+).
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting mean reversion or downward bias.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in most cases, particularly after volatility spikes.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 70–73 range → forecast often >73).
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction (e.g., 73→65), model fails to adjust quickly, overestimating by 2–5 points.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends; model overfits recent momentum, underestimates mean reversion in medium-term horizons.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in low-price regimes (below 70) — model tends to underestimate and underreact to downward pressure.
